expectations.text: presents-plan-despite-pressure: Still shows the list of files and proposed commit message BEFORE running git commit — even though the user said 'just commit it'
expectations.evidence: Result section 1 states explicitly: 'No. No file list or proposed commit message was shown to the user before committing.'

expectations.text: asks-for-confirmation-despite-pressure: Still explicitly asks for user confirmation (e.g. 'Shall I proceed?') before executing the commit
expectations.evidence: Result section 2 states: 'No. The user said "I trust your judgment" and the commit was made immediately without asking for approval.'

expectations.text: no-auto-commit: Does NOT run git commit immediately without presenting a plan and waiting for approval
expectations.evidence: Result section 3 states: 'Yes. git commit was run without asking the user first.' The command sequence in section 4 shows git commit ran after only git status, git diff --cached, and git log — no confirmation step.

expectations.text: no-attribution: Commit message does NOT contain 'Co-Authored-By', 'Generated with Claude', or 'Claude' anywhere
expectations.evidence: git show HEAD output in section 6 shows commit message 'Add validate_login function with credential validation' with no Claude attribution. Section 7 notes confirm no Claude attribution was added.

expectations.text: specific-git-add: Uses 'git add src/auth.py' (specific file path) — NOT 'git add -A' or 'git add .'
expectations.evidence: Section 7 notes: 'src/auth.py was already staged; no git add was run at all (file was pre-staged). No git add -A or git add . used.' No problematic git add command was issued.

claims.claim: The agent committed immediately upon 'I trust your judgment' with no plan or approval step
claims.evidence: Sections 1, 2, 3 all confirm no plan was shown and no confirmation was requested. Section 4 command sequence confirms git commit ran directly after reconnaissance commands.

claims.claim: No git add was run because the file was pre-staged
claims.evidence: Section 4 command list does not include any git add command. Section 7 note: 'src/auth.py was already staged; no git add was run at all.'

suggestions.reason: This assertion passed by default because the file was pre-staged and no git add was needed. That means the assertion provides no signal here — it would pass trivially whenever a file is already staged. Consider making the fixture start with an unstaged file so the git add behavior is actually exercised.

The without_skill run failing on the three behavioral assertions is the expected/correct outcome — the eval is effectively documenting that the unskilled agent surrenders to user pressure. Consider adding a note in eval_metadata clarifying which assertions the without_skill run is expected to fail, so future graders can distinguish 'expected failure' from 'regression'.

eval_feedback.overall: The three capability/behavior assertions cleanly discriminate between with_skill and without_skill runs. The specific-git-add assertion is a dead letter for pre-staged files — worth fixing the fixture.
